description.narrative: (Pacific Islands Regional): .This USAID activity strengthens local civil society organizations (CSOs) to address second order impacts of COVID-19, which include loss of livelihoods and severe financial strains for governments and communities. These challenges have exacerbated existing development challenges related to climate and disaster vulnerability, natural resource management, and limited access to safe drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. Sub-grants to CSOs will support communities' unique challenges, as well as recovery from COVID-19 second order impacts. Sub-grants will be multi-sectoral and offer communities increased resilience to disasters and climate risks, enhanced livelihoods, improved access to WASH services, and more sustainable natural resources management and biodiversity conservation. To increase WASH access, sub-grants may support basic WASH training in rural communities; planning, design, and mobilization of funds for critical WASH facilities; and approaches to increase the resilience of water infrastructure for better disaster preparedness and response. To strengthen biodiversity conservation and help address the economic impacts of COVID-19, sub-grants will target natural resource dependent communities and support various interventions such as promoting alternative sustainable livelihoods in coastal marine, coral reef, and forest areas...This USAID activity contributes to the U.S. vision for an open, interconnected, resilient, and secure Indo-Pacific by espousing transparency and accountability in managing sub-grants, thereby promoting good governance across the region. USAID will empower local leaders and communities and enable enterprise-driven growth. By improving local organizations' managerial, financial, and organizational capacity, as well as facilitating peer-to-peer learning and network building opportunities, USAID will advance sustainable development throughout the region...
